dispatch.summary:
I'm approving T415 (91d2f6c0 against fe1508d3). It meets every acceptance item and changes no engine or web code. I didn't run any tests myself because this review session is read-only. The runner's own check passed: typecheck, lint, format:check and `vitest --changed` (98 files, 810 tests), all under the default config. The worker reports that worlds.test.ts also passes (4 tests) under the release-on config; the runner didn't run that, and I checked it by reading the code instead.

The risk reason was the autopilot decision of 2026-10-24 that is still waiting for the owner: every test names its release, and a release-on vitest config checks each file with the switch both on and off. The change follows that decision exactly, adds no new planning decisions, and only touches test setup, so it doesn't lock out the alternatives.

What I checked in the code:
- `DISABLED_RELEASE` and `ENABLED_RELEASE` are copies of the release object, so they keep their own on/off value whatever the switch is.
- `simulatedWorld(input, span, release = MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE)` puts the release in its cache ID and passes it through every nested build. The engine only reads the release in `createWorld` and the host constructor, and season rollover never reads it, so a world built with a given release stays on that release.
- `cached` reads `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` when it runs and adds it to the key for both the memory and the disk cache.
- The engine's release object isn't frozen, and the setup file and the tests import the same object.
- `vitest.release-on.config.ts` merges the base config, which has no setupFiles, workspaces or projects. The tsconfig includes root `*.ts` files and allows `.ts` imports. The `package.json` script matches the acceptance text exactly.
- The cache-separation test flips the switch inside one case and restores it in `finally`. That is safe because cases in a file run one after another and the base config keeps each file in its own worker. The task notes say only the setup file should change the switch; this test-only flip goes beyond that, but the worker disclosed it, it is scoped to one case, and it proves the separation within a single run.

There are two optional suggestions and nothing that needs fixing.

findings.message: The global `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` goes into every cache key, including `simulatedWorld` calls that pass an explicit release. Those worlds don't depend on the global switch, so the switch-off and release-on runs can't share them. That includes the `DISABLED_RELEASE` worlds that T417 will use for most shared engine worlds. Running both test tiers therefore builds and stores each of these worlds twice, which matters given the known problem of the world cache filling the disk. This follows the acceptance as written and doesn't affect T420's cold-vs-cold gate. Optional, for T420 to weigh against its warm timings: hash the effective release instead, i.e. the explicit one for `simulatedWorld` and the default for `cachedWorld`.

The test "simulatedWorld pins the release it is given" only covers a world on its founding day. If the release were dropped from the nested `simulatedWorld(…, release)` calls for seasons or rounds, the default would quietly take over, and none of the tests would catch it under either config. Optional: add a cheap case such as `simulatedWorld(input, { rounds: 1 }, DISABLED_RELEASE).matchModel` toBeUndefined, which fails under the release-on config if the release isn't passed down.

dispatch.summary:
T418 (e04a04aa against base fada6e6d, merge-base 2737e84a) changes only the seven touched test files and the task file. No runtime or adapter source changed. Neither risk reason is a problem in T418: (1) 301 lines is one over the 300-line limit, and most of the count is the SAVE-24 main case re-indented into `it.each`; (2) the autopilot decision waiting on the owner is T416's, on the group board, and this attempt has none of its own. The commits between the merge-base and the base (T417/T416, engine grid tests) don't overlap these files.

Acceptance 1 is met. Pre-model fixtures now build with `DISABLED_RELEASE`: legacyReset `saved`, matchModelPacking `career`, the container-selection case in managerHistoryPacking, the untracked case in persistence.history, persistence `unmodelled` for the container-1/2 cases, the `modelCareer` bases and the failed-write predecessor, client `legacyCheckpoint`/`identitylessCheckpoint`/`preModelCheckpoint`, and host `preIdentity`/model-block `career`/`older`. The shared `preIdentityCareer()` sits outside this task's touches; persistence.test strips its model explicitly with `withoutMatchModel`, which removes the same three fields that `carriesMatchModel` checks. Every case that loads a career as the writer (identity adoption, combined upgrades, the ledger read, the recorded-model load, SAVE-24 tracking) now builds its host with an explicit `release`, either directly or through `WorkerPort.release`, which `beforeEach` resets. The cases left on the default host only do read-only loads, inspections or compatibility refusals, so they don't depend on the switch.

Acceptance 2 is met. The default-host founding expects `founding` coverage exactly when `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` is true, and the exact-inspection metadata carries `source.matchModel` with an exact presence check. Coverage also got wider: 'moves the revision once' now runs with the release on and asserts `matchModel.activated.revision === 10`, and the main SAVE-24 case runs under both releases.

These rules follow T402 (no load gate; activation only on the writer path) and the 261024 decision that every test names its release. I checked the codec's container ordering (`readCheckpoint`) to confirm the schema-2 damage cases left on the default world hold in both switch states.

Verification: the runner's task check (typecheck, lint, format:check, `vitest --changed`: 7 files, 157 passed) covers the switch-off state only. The release-on run (157 passed) and the build are the worker's own claims. I didn't re-run either: the review checkout has no node_modules, and installing them would change the checkout. T420 and the unit gate run the release-on tier. The worker handed the browser specs that assume the switch is off to T286, as the impl notes ask.

findings.message: `writer()` defaults to `DISABLED_RELEASE`, so three SAVE-24 cases test only a host with the release off: 'waits for a queued or revealed own match before tracking starts' (:1091), 'never tracks from a read-only load or an inspection' (:1113) and 'keeps the previous checkpoint and the tracked career exportable when the write fails' (:1125). Only the main case runs under both releases. Once T286 flips the switch, a writer loading an older career will record the model and start tracking in the same activation. Nothing here proves those two upgrades wait for the same safe boundary and survive a failed write together, beyond T402's model-only cases. Optional follow-up for T420/T286: run the queued and failed-write cases under `it.each([DISABLED_RELEASE, ENABLED_RELEASE])` too.

findings.message: The new `expect(s.matchModel!.coverage).toBe('founding')` would also pass if the default switch had activated the model when createWorld founded the world: that is the earlier-boundary case this task removes, since activation then also happens at round 0 with no own matches. So it doesn't prove what the comment says ('Only the explicit release activated'). Assert the boundary too, e.g. `expect(s.matchModel!.activated.year).toBe(2024)` or the `trackedFrom` year, so the case fails if the activation ever comes from the default again.

With an enabled release, `founded(year, release)` records the model at createWorld's founding and only then moves the year and calls prepareSeason. The docstring documents this, but it gives an inconsistent world: activated and trackedFrom sit before `year`. After T286 flips the default, every other importer gets that world: cups, discipline, full-model-throughput and season.brackets/contracts/exchange/groups/professional. Option: create the world disabled and, when `release.enabled`, call `activateMatchModel(w, release)` after prepareSeason. Then `founded(year, ENABLED_RELEASE)` would mean a candidate founded in `year`. Otherwise, hand this trap to T420 explicitly.

The new-career replay now plays the candidate model in the default unit run too (ENABLED_RELEASE), but the comment still says it 'takes about 11 s and keeps the config's limit'. That figure was measured on the pre-feature path, and the candidate's seasons are slower (T285). The result records no time for this case on either config. Refresh the figure, or note it for T420's timing table, so the default run's cost and timeout margin stay known.

T415 구현을 마쳤습니다. 커밋과 제출은 호스트 러너 몫으로 남겨 두었습니다. 엔진과 웹 코드는 손대지 않았습니다.

- `tests/fixtures/worlds.ts`: `ENABLED_RELEASE` 옆에 `DISABLED_RELEASE`를 추가했습니다. `simulatedWorld(input, span, release = MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE)`는 받은 release를 `createWorld`와 하위 시즌/라운드 빌드까지 넘기고, 캐시 id에도 붙입니다. `cached`는 호출 시점의 `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled`를 모든 캐시 키에 넣으므로, 스위치를 끈 채 만든 월드가 스위치를 켠 실행에 쓰이지 않습니다. 기존 디스크 캐시는 한 번씩 다시 빌드됩니다.
- `tests/setup/release-on.ts`: 엔진의 `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled`를 켭니다. readonly 캐스트는 이 setup 파일에만 둡니다.

review.summary:
I'm approving T415 (91d2f6c0 against fe1508d3). It meets every acceptance item and changes no engine or web code. I didn't run any tests myself because this review session is read-only. The runner's own check passed: typecheck, lint, format:check and `vitest --changed` (98 files, 810 tests), all under the default config. The worker reports that worlds.test.ts also passes (4 tests) under the release-on config; the runner didn't run that, and I checked it by reading the code instead.

The risk reason was the autopilot decision of 2026-10-24 that is still waiting for the owner: every test names its release, and a release-on vitest config checks each file with the switch both on and off. The change follows that decision exactly, adds no new planning decisions, and only touches test setup, so it doesn't lock out the alternatives.

What I checked in the code:
- `DISABLED_RELEASE` and `ENABLED_RELEASE` are copies of the release object, so they keep their own on/off value whatever the switch is.
- `simulatedWorld(input, span, release = MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE)` puts the release in its cache ID and passes it through every nested build. The engine only reads the release in `createWorld` and the host constructor, and season rollover never reads it, so a world built with a given release stays on that release.
- `cached` reads `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` when it runs and adds it to the key for both the memory and the disk cache.
- The engine's release object isn't frozen, and the setup file and the tests import the same object.
- `vitest.release-on.config.ts` merges the base config, which has no setupFiles, workspaces or projects. The tsconfig includes root `*.ts` files and allows `.ts` imports. The `package.json` script matches the acceptance text exactly.
- The cache-separation test flips the switch inside one case and restores it in `finally`. That is safe because cases in a file run one after another and the base config keeps each file in its own worker. The task notes say only the setup file should change the switch; this test-only flip goes beyond that, but the worker disclosed it, it is scoped to one case, and it proves the separation within a single run.

There are two optional suggestions and nothing that needs fixing.

findings.message: The global `MATCH_MODEL_RELEASE.enabled` goes into every cache key, including `simulatedWorld` calls that pass an explicit release. Those worlds don't depend on the global switch, so the switch-off and release-on runs can't share them. That includes the `DISABLED_RELEASE` worlds that T417 will use for most shared engine worlds. Running both test tiers therefore builds and stores each of these worlds twice, which matters given the known problem of the world cache filling the disk. This follows the acceptance as written and doesn't affect T420's cold-vs-cold gate. Optional, for T420 to weigh against its warm timings: hash the effective release instead, i.e. the explicit one for `simulatedWorld` and the default for `cachedWorld`.

The test "simulatedWorld pins the release it is given" only covers a world on its founding day. If the release were dropped from the nested `simulatedWorld(…, release)` calls for seasons or rounds, the default would quietly take over, and none of the tests would catch it under either config. Optional: add a cheap case such as `simulatedWorld(input, { rounds: 1 }, DISABLED_RELEASE).matchModel` toBeUndefined, which fails under the release-on config if the release isn't passed down.

- **What reads the clock.** Goal feedback and `Pitch.tsx` (seeking, progress bar, possession cue) now use match seconds. The old `presentationLength`, `clockAt` and `runningSeconds` are gone. `possessionCue.ts` already took seconds and is unchanged.
- **Test hook.** The pitch canvas exposes the current match second as `data-seconds`, so browser journeys can time the clock.

**One departure from the impl note.** The note says the kick is the restart event's own time. On both models that time is actually when the delivery lands, so following it would also speed up the delivery, which WEB-32 and MATCH-12 keep at the selected speed. Instead the kick is read from data both models carry:
- pre-feature: the moment the taker takes the ball, from `holders`
- candidate: its recorded kick sample, the last sample with phase 'restart'

Either must fall more than 0.1 s before the landing, so a taker passing to himself isn't read as the kick. On the pre-feature this gives the note's own "32 s dead, 3.2 s kick". This doesn't change the spec, so I didn't raise it as a blocker.

**Measured on the real engine** (four seeded first matches per model):
- Every corner, free kick and goal kick got a preparation.
- Deliveries stay at running speed (0.15–5.6 s).
- A whole match takes about 14.3–15.9 min at 1x and 8.0–8.6 min at 2x, down from 19 and 9.5. That is slightly longer than WEB-32's "about 13–14 / 7 minutes"; it's for your in-play review of the 1500 ms value.

**Checks that passed:** the three affected test files (38 tests), typecheck, lint, format:check, `vitest run --changed d1ae3485` (4 files, 50 tests) and the build.

**Not run (batch):**
- `set-piece-defence.spec.ts` (candidate scene) and a new test in `stable-controls-and-pacing.spec.ts` (pre-feature, seed `stable-pace`). Both seek to just before a dead ball, resume at 1x, and check the preparation is drawn in 1.4–2.5 s with the players still moving and no jumps.
- They share a new helper, `tests/e2e/preparation.ts`, which is outside touches.
- The existing pace journeys still need the batch run too.

The task result records all of this.

findings.message: `writer()` defaults to `DISABLED_RELEASE`, so three SAVE-24 cases test only a host with the release off: 'waits for a queued or revealed own match before tracking starts' (:1091), 'never tracks from a read-only load or an inspection' (:1113) and 'keeps the previous checkpoint and the tracked career exportable when the write fails' (:1125). Only the main case runs under both releases. Once T286 flips the switch, a writer loading an older career will record the model and start tracking in the same activation. Nothing here proves those two upgrades wait for the same safe boundary and survive a failed write together, beyond T402's model-only cases. Optional follow-up for T420/T286: run the queued and failed-write cases under `it.each([DISABLED_RELEASE, ENABLED_RELEASE])` too.

findings.message: The new `expect(s.matchModel!.coverage).toBe('founding')` would also pass if the default switch had activated the model when createWorld founded the world: that is the earlier-boundary case this task removes, since activation then also happens at round 0 with no own matches. So it doesn't prove what the comment says ('Only the explicit release activated'). Assert the boundary too, e.g. `expect(s.matchModel!.activated.year).toBe(2024)` or the `trackedFrom` year, so the case fails if the activation ever comes from the default again.

With an enabled release, `founded(year, release)` records the model at createWorld's founding and only then moves the year and calls prepareSeason. The docstring documents this, but it gives an inconsistent world: activated and trackedFrom sit before `year`. After T286 flips the default, every other importer gets that world: cups, discipline, full-model-throughput and season.brackets/contracts/exchange/groups/professional. Option: create the world disabled and, when `release.enabled`, call `activateMatchModel(w, release)` after prepareSeason. Then `founded(year, ENABLED_RELEASE)` would mean a candidate founded in `year`. Otherwise, hand this trap to T420 explicitly.

The new-career replay now plays the candidate model in the default unit run too (ENABLED_RELEASE), but the comment still says it 'takes about 11 s and keeps the config's limit'. That figure was measured on the pre-feature path, and the candidate's seasons are slower (T285). The result records no time for this case on either config. Refresh the figure, or note it for T420's timing table, so the default run's cost and timeout margin stay known.
